body.p: Coyote was going along somewhere. He was approaching a cave near which, apparently, a cotton-tail rabbit was lying or standingThe use of irrealis mood in these verbal clauses are motivated by the uncertainty of the situation.. Rabbit spotted Coyote coming, and in his fright, not knowing what Coyote would say to him, he quickly raised his paws to the ceiling of the cave and stood there pushing up on it.
Now, Coyote just wanted to eat the rabbit. He saw what Rabbit was doing, but he didn't understand why.

Rabbit said to Coyote (already tricking him): "I'm standing here pushing up on the ceiling of this cave. The moment that I were to stop pushing up on it, the Catastrophe would happen. So that is why I am standing here pushing up on the ceiling of this cave."

Coyote was frightened when he heard that, and ran off. Rabbit also ran away. He had tricked him.This is one example where a nominalization is used to refer to an event that is off the timeline of the narrative. This sentence recapitulates what had already happened.
